title: Can Agents Keep Secrets They Were Never Told? Benchmarking Latent Privacy Risks Across Sessions with MemJoin
abstract: arXiv:2610.24359v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: To support sustained interactions and personalized assistance, agents use long-term memory to retain and combine user information across sessions. Reusing such memories can lead an agent to state a sensitive relation while completing an ordinary task that does not require it. The relation to protect and the combination of clues that reveal it may remain hidden at memory write time, when later records and tasks are still unknown. In this paper, we introduce MemJoin, a privacy benchmark of 288 synthetic analysis cases in which the complete history entails a sensitive relation, but every individual session is insufficient. We evaluate six memory systems with the same answer-generating model, alongside full-history and no-history controls. translated_title: 智能体能否保守它们从未被告知的秘密？基于MemJoin的跨会话潜在隐私风险基准测试
translated_abstract: 为了支持持续交互和个性化辅助，智能体使用长期记忆来跨会话保留和组合用户信息。重复使用此类记忆可能导致智能体在完成一项并不需要该信息的普通任务时，无意中说出某种敏感关系。需要保护的关系以及揭示该关系的线索组合，在写入记忆时可能仍然隐匿，因为后续的记录和任务当时尚不可知。本文提出了MemJoin，一个包含288个合成分析案例的隐私基准，其中完整的历史记录蕴含某种敏感关系，但任何单个会话都不足以揭示它。我们使用相同的答案生成模型评估了六种记忆系统，并设置了全历史和无历史对照组。每个系统按会话顺序写入和更新记忆，随后为普通任务检索上下文，同时目标标注始终仅由评估方持有。我们分别检查哪些目标属（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出MemJoin隐私基准，揭示智能体长期记忆系统会通过跨会话组合碎片化线索，在执行普通任务时泄露用户从未被明确告知的敏感关系。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MemJoin, a privacy benchmark of 288 cases showing that agents' long-term memory systems can leak sensitive user relations across sessions by combining clues that no individual session alone reveals.
